decisions.reason: As a narrow agricultural crate with only modest observed market prominence and four years for demand to reveal itself, its remaining upside looks limited relative to the value of freeing capacity for stronger options.

The foldable large container had dedicated visibility in both observed years and sits close to the firm's core industrial handling portfolio, making it a relatively low-cost option worth keeping open.
A stackable plastic crate fits standard plastic logistics products and likely shares customers and production assets, so the firm can keep it with limited downside while preserving potential demand.
The medium-duty rackable pallet is closely related to the established pallet range, so carrying it remains a cheap and sensible option unless clearer weak sales evidence emerges.
Although the spill-retention pallet lost website prominence after launch, it still extends the pallet portfolio into a specialized compliance niche where keeping the option open is not very costly.

The plastic pallet with load retainers appears to have weakened in prominence after launch and may overlap with existing pallet offerings, so by now the option value likely no longer justifies portfolio complexity.
